fields.name: tailSize
fields.evidence: Create computes the trailing-array size n and calls FastAlloc(n+0x40); ctor (unnamed FUN_00076fe0) stores n at +0; operator_delete(p,sz) does FastFree(p, *p + sz) and callers pass sz=0x40. PS2 identical (sw a3,0(s1); operator delete lw v0,0(a0))

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: RSceneObj::UseInstanceList passes this as Create's last arg -> ctor +4; RWorldCamera passes 0. System::Update calls owner->vtable[0x2c]; ctor reads owner+0x10 (baseDesc) for CalcDamageZone; PS2 SetEventDynamicData reads owner+0x3c = PS2 RSceneObj vptr

fields.name: procAnims
fields.evidence: ctor: array of numProcAnims 0x20-byte records copied from Create's ProcAnimState table (index = instance ushort +0xe, which is rewritten to the local index); placed after the effects array. Type name from PS2 CreatePathHandle(CARP::Instance &, CARP::ProcAnimS..; no reader seen besides the ctor

fields.name: systems
fields.evidence: 0x40-byte System records, count +0x1e; ctor sets sys->handle=this and state bytes +0x14..+0x1d; IsSystemPlaying/GetSystemState/SetFrame/PS2 FindSystem index it by lower_bound position in systemIds. Existing Ghidra name pSystems

fields.name: systemIds
fields.evidence: sorted byte array (lower_bound<unsigned char>) of numSystems system IDs, the last trailing array; ctor fills it from sys+0x15. Existing Ghidra name pSystemIds

fields.name: effects
fields.evidence: first trailing array after the instances (this+(numInstances+1)*0x40), numEffects 0x40-byte effect records copied from the anim descriptor; FindEffectByID returns effects+i*0x40; RSceneObj Toggle/Trigger/Damage/Decay/SuppressEffects walk it (+0x10 flags, +0x14 type, +0x1c GFX handle). Effect type name assumed

fields.name: effectBits
fields.evidence: PS2/Xbox SetEffectBits(i,v) stores a ushort at +0x18[i]; DamageEffects/TriggerEffects mask against it. The byte array of effect IDs follows it in the same block: FindEffectByID reads byte effectBits+2*numEffects+i

fields.name: numInstances
fields.evidence: ctor stores Create's instance count; tail starts at this+(n+1)*0x40; UseInstanceList loops instances [0,n) at this+0x40 stride 0x40. PS2 sb t0,0x1c

fields.name: numProcAnims
fields.evidence: ctor: count of 0x20-byte procAnims records (Create counts instances with flag 0x10 when a ProcAnimState table is given)

fields.name: numSystems
fields.evidence: loop bound in InitAllSystemStates/AnySystemPlaying/ProcessStimuli*; length for lower_bound on systemIds. Existing Ghidra name bSystemCount

fields.name: numEffects
fields.evidence: FindEffectByID and all RSceneObj effect loops are bounded by it

fields.name: activeEffectMask
fields.evidence: ToggleEffect sets/clears bit i; Trigger/Damage/Decay/RenderEffects test it !=0 to arm/clear RSceneObj.effectDecayTime; ctor zeroes it (PS2 sd zero,0x20)

fields.name: damageEffectMask
fields.evidence: ctor ORs bit i when effect flags &8; DamageEffects early-outs unless nonzero and toggles only those effects

fields.name: gfxEffectMask
fields.evidence: ctor ORs bit i when effect type byte (+0x14) == 6; ToggleEffect calls GFX::Trigger/Purge only for effects in this mask (otherwise it only flips activeEffectMask); SuppressEffects/DecayEffects filter on it. Name invented

fields.name: triggerEffectMask
fields.evidence: ctor ORs bit i when effect flags &0x96; TriggerEffects/SuppressEffects early-out unless nonzero and act only on its bits that are not damage bits. Name invented

fields.name: instance
fields.evidence: (Instance&,ProcAnimState&) ctor stores arg1; GetPosition returns instance+0x30, GetOrientMat copies *instance; Update reads instance+0x30..0x38 for velocity; RPathEngine::GetPathHandle(instance) matches on it. Same on PS2

fields.name: procAnim
fields.evidence: ctor arg2 (0x20-byte record, type byte 2): Init reads +0xc path, +0x10 master id, +0x14 start time, +0x18 speed, +0x1c flag, +4 bit15 running; Update/Init call the vtable[0x38] of the object at procAnim+8

fields.name: baseMatrix
fields.evidence: ctor copies the 16 instance words, then zeroes words 3/7/11 and sets [15]=1.0 (instance w-lanes carry packed data); Init/Update MatrixCopy(this+8) before EvaluateMatrix. Same offset on PS2 (unaligned ldl/ldr copy, no padding)

fields.name: applyMatrix
fields.evidence: Init sets it to identity (DAT_001917b0) or through VU0_MATRIX4Init when procAnim+0x1c is set; Update/Init post-multiply the evaluated path matrix by it. Name invented

fields.name: velocity
fields.evidence: Update: (newPos - instance+0x30)*k; ctor/Init set it from zero vector DAT_00243030; RSceneObj::GetVelocity and EPathSFXUpdate (sound velocity +0x20) read it. 12 bytes on PS2 too (+0x94 is the next field)

fields.name: lastUpdateTime
fields.evidence: Init/Update store scale*t*60; Update returns early when now - this <= 0. PS2 lwc1/swc1 0x94

fields.name: currentPath
fields.evidence: PS2 SetCurrentPath = sw 0x98; GetParametricDuration returns *(float*)currentPath (duration at PathInfo+0); Update wraps time against it; Init sets it from procAnim+0xc

fields.name: nextPath
fields.evidence: SetNextPath = store 0x9c (both builds); Update switches currentPath to it when time passes the end

fields.name: masterHandle
fields.evidence: Init looks up the handle whose instance == procAnim+0x10 in the global list (node+8); Update then derives time from master->parametricTime; SetParametricTime is ignored while set; WTriggerManager::Update only processes handles with 0 here

fields.name: speed
fields.evidence: PS2 SetSpeed = swc1 0xa4 (no Xbox SetSpeed); Init from procAnim+0x18; Update multiplies throttle*speed*dt

fields.name: timeDelta
fields.evidence: Update stores throttle*speed*dt here when free-running, and uses time = master->parametricTime - this when slaved; Init sets master time - own time. Dual use, name invented

fields.name: parametricTime
fields.evidence: SetParametricTime stores 0xac (both builds); passed to EvaluateMatrix/ComputeChannel; Init from procAnim+0x14

fields.name: posKnot
fields.evidence: EvaluateMatrix in/out knot hint for the position channel (EvaluateLinear/Spline return the knot index); copy ctor zeroes it (both builds)

fields.name: rotKnot
fields.evidence: EvaluateMatrix in/out knot hint for the rotation channel; copy ctor zeroes it

fields.name: pathW
fields.evidence: EvaluateMatrix out: 4th lane of the evaluated position channel (0 when there is no channel). Meaning unknown, name invented

fields.name: throttle
fields.evidence: SetThrottle stores 0xbc (both builds); Init 1.0; Update ramps it toward desiredThrottle by acceleration

fields.name: acceleration
fields.evidence: SetAcceleration stores 0xc0; Init 1.0; Update step size

fields.name: desiredThrottle
fields.evidence: SetDesiredThrottle stores 0xc4; Init 1.0; Update target

fields.name: accelDelay
fields.evidence: SetAccelDelay stores 0xc8 (decompiler prints it as decimal 200; PS2 integer sw); Update decrements it and ramps only once it is 0

fields.name: running
fields.evidence: SetRunning byte store on Xbox; Init = procAnim flags bit15; Update skips when 0 and clears it at path end. PS2 stores a WORD here (sw a1,0xcc; ctor and copy ctor move a word): Xbox is 1 byte + 3 padding

fields.name: userData
fields.evidence: ctor default &SMissionManager::glbMissionManager (PS2 DAT_00381f68); CreatePathHandle sets it to (*(instance+0x1c))+0x34, AISplinePath ctor/Reset to spline+0x44. No reader found among path-engine callers on either build; meaning unknown

gotchas: Neither class has a vtable, so there is NO +4 shift: every RAnimEngine::Handle and RPathHandle field sits at the same offset on PS2 and Xbox. A script must decide 'has a vtable' per class (the ctor stores a vtable constant at +0 on Xbox, or at the end on PS2) before shifting, and must never default to +4.

The Vec3/matrix padding rule is not universal: RPathHandle's MATRIX4s at +0x8/+0x48 are copied with unaligned ldl/ldr on PS2 (they are not 16-aligned) and its COORD3 at +0x88 is 12 bytes on PS2 (+0x94 is the next float). Padding depends on the declared type (VU0 qword types vs COORD3/float[3]), so check each member instead of applying a blanket drift per Vec3.

Variable-size object: RAnimEngine::Handle is a 0x40 header plus trailing arrays (instances at +0x40 stride 0x40, then effects, procAnims, systems, effectBits+effect IDs, systemIds) in one FastAlloc(n+0x40) block. The allocation size is a runtime value, not sizeof. Take the size from the constant passed to operator_delete(p,0x40) (PS2 ~Handle passes 0x40); header+0x0 stores the tail size n.

STL container nodes inflate allocation sizes: RPathHandles live in a std::list. FastAlloc(0xdc,"STL") and FastFree(node,0xdc) cover node(next,prev)+0xd4, and every handle pointer is node+8. The real size (0xd4) comes from PS2 operator= memcpy(0xd4) or the copy ctor's extent.

The Xbox Handle constructor is unnamed (FUN_00076fe0, called only from Handle::Create); PS2 has Handle::Handle. A script that finds ctors by name misses the most informative function; it should follow the callees of Create/operator new.

An existing too-small Ghidra struct corrupts decompiler offsets: with the 32-byte RAnimEngine::Handle applied, +0x20 prints as *(uint*)(pHVar1+1), +0x24 as pHVar1[1].field_0x4, +0x30 as pHVar2[1].pSystemIds, +0x4c as pHVar5[2].pSystems and instance i+0x1c as this[i*2+2].field_0x1c. Take offsets from disassembly/p-code (or strip the type first), never by parsing decompiler text.

64-bit fields on MSVC x86 are accessed as two dwords (EAX/EDX pairs at +0x20/+0x24, and so on), and the bit tests go through __allshl/__aullshr helpers whose arguments the decompiler drops (__aullshr() with no args). Access-width inference yields two uints. PS2 uses sd/ld (8 bytes), so merge the pair using the PS2 width or the EAX/EDX pattern.

Access widths for bools differ between builds: RPathHandle.running is a byte store on Xbox (SetRunning, copy ctor byte) but a word store on PS2 (sw a1,0xcc; the ctor and copy ctor move a full word). Take sizes from Xbox, not PS2.

One pointer field can address two arrays: Handle+0x18 is ushort effectBits[n] (SetEffectBits), directly followed by byte effectIds[n], which FindEffectByID reads at +0x18 base + 2n + i. Access-based typing sees both ushort and byte element reads through +0x18.

Accessor names do not always name a field of this class. RPathHandle::GetPosition returns instance(+0x0)+0x30 and GetOrientMat copies *instance, so both describe the pointee, not a 'position' member. GetParametricDuration returns *(float*)(this+0x98), so +0x98 is currentPath (PathInfo*, duration at its +0), not a float 'parametricDuration'. Only a single direct load/store of this+X counts as a getter/setter.
Conditional setters exist: SetParametricTime stores +0xac only if +0xa0 == 0. A strict 'one store, then return' setter matcher misses it; a looser one should still name only the stored offset.

Some accessors exist on only one build: PS2 has SetCurrentPath (+0x98), SetSpeed (+0xa4), FindChannelByName/GetChannelName/ComputeChannel, and Handle::FindSystem/InitSystemState/HideSystem/ShowSystem/SetVerbose/GetSystemStartTick..., which Xbox inlined or dropped. Carry names over from PS2 by offset (identical here), not by matching Xbox functions.

Decompiler casts lie about float fields when 'this' is typed int*: RPathHandle::Update shows param_1_00[0x2f] = (int)(float...) and param_1_00[0x2b] = (int)fVar4. Infer float from FPU instructions (FLD/FSTP, PS2 lwc1/swc1), not from the decompiler's casts.
Offsets are not always hex in decompiler output: SetAccelDelay writes *(this + 200) (0xc8). Regexes that only match 0x.. miss decimal offsets; use disassembly.

A constant stored by the ctor is not the field's type: RPathHandle+0xd0 is initialised to &SMissionManager::glbMissionManager but later set to AISpline+0x44 or (*(instance+0x1c))+0x34. Typing it from the symbol at the stored address would wrongly give SMissionManager*.

Struct copies hide field boundaries: the copy ctor copies +0x8..+0x88 as two 16-dword REP MOVS blocks on Xbox (ldl/ldr/sdl/sdr pairs on PS2), and the plain ctor zeroes words 5/9/13 inside the matrix. Word-level accesses inside copies must not create 4-byte fields inside a known MATRIX4.

Some fields are reached only through callee arguments: +0xb0/+0xb4/+0xb8 are only ever passed by address to CARP::PathInfo::EvaluateMatrix (in/out knot hints and an out float). Their types come from how the callee uses the pointer parameter, not from accesses in the caller (the copy ctor only zeroes them).

Some offsets are reached only via stride arithmetic: Handle instance nodes are addressed as this + (idx+1)*0x40 + k or this + idx*0x40 + 0x5c. A script must not turn +0x40.., +0x4c or +0x5c into header fields past the 0x40 header size.
notes: RAnimEngine::Handle trailing block order (Xbox ctor FUN_00076fe0 / PS2 0x1a1f58): +0x40 CARP::Instance copies [numInstances] (0x40 each; instance+0xe is rewritten to the local procAnim index), then effects [numEffects] x 0x40 (+0x14), procAnims [numProcAnims] x 0x20 (+0x8), systems [numSystems] x 0x40 (+0xc), effectBits ushort[numEffects] (+0x18), effect IDs byte[numEffects], and systemIds byte[numSystems] (+0x10). Create's size formula: numProcAnims*0x20 + numSystems*0x41 + numEffects*0x43 + numInstances*0x40, plus the 0x40 header.

The existing Ghidra /RAnimEngine/Handle (32 bytes) names pSystems (+0xc), pSystemIds (+0x10) and bSystemCount (+0x1e); this JSON renames them systems/systemIds/numSystems. Keep the old names if other code depends on them.

System record (0x40, RAnimEngine::System) fields seen in passing: +0x0 Handle* back pointer, +0xc ushort damage-zone mask (ProcessStimuliZones), +0x15 system id, +0x16 state, +0x17 initial state, +0x19 playing, +0x1a numInstances, +0x1b min frame count (init 100), +0x1c verbose, +0x1e.. byte instance indices.
RPathHandle is also the payload of the global list DAT_001ec300 (std::list header: +4 sentinel node, +8 count); GetFirst/GetNextPathHandle and GetPathHandle return node+8.

The type names CARP::Effect (effect record) and CARP::ProcAnimState (procAnim) are assumed: the PS2 sheet name is cut at 63 chars ('CARP::ProcAnimS...'). Check them against the existing Ghidra data types before applying.
Invented names (no PS2 accessor behind them): tailSize, owner, procAnims, the four effect masks, applyMatrix, velocity, lastUpdateTime, masterHandle, timeDelta, posKnot, rotKnot, pathW, userData.
